### <span class="imp imp-high" title="Importance 7/10" aria-label="Importance 7 of 10">7</span> Stolen AI accounts emerge as underground commodity amid rising LLM account theft
Cybersecurity researchers report that stolen credentials for premium AI services including Claude, Gemini, and Cursor Pro are increasingly traded on dark web marketplaces. Average prices for compromised AI accounts more than doubled in 2026, reflecting growing criminal demand to bypass subscription costs and access expensive models.

<ul class="takeaways">
<li>Stolen Claude, Gemini, Cursor Pro, and Devin credentials most heavily traded</li>
<li>Average prices for stolen AI accounts doubled in 2026 compared to prior year</li>
<li>Infostealer malware increasingly targeting AI service credentials</li>
<li>Criminals use stolen accounts for automating phishing, malware development, and credential theft</li>
<li>Coding-assistant credentials highly attractive for software analysis and modification</li>
</ul>
